correctness.rationale: The pointwise hypothesis defines an everywhere-defined linear analysis map into a Hilbert direct sum. Its graph is closed because all coordinate maps are bounded, so the closed graph theorem gives the uniform unweighted Bessel bound \(B_0\). The resolution identity yields \(\|f\|^2=\sum_jv_ja_j\); Cauchy–Schwarz gives the lower bound \(1/B_0\), and \(v_j\le M\) gives the upper bound \(M\). Explicit scalar one- and two-atom families verify universal sharpness for every admissible \(MB_0\ge1\).
